title: Probabilistic degradation budget and smart circuit thresholds for multi-region endpoints
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Define and implement a probabilistic SLO decomposition and corresponding circuit-breaker thresholds that allow graceful, measurable degradation across multi-region model endpoints. This ticket scopes: (1) an SLI/SLO schema that separates availability (latency/timeout) and quality (model correctness/acceptance) per endpoint+model variant, (2) a probabilistic error budget allocator that reserves/borrows capacity across regions and variants, (3) a set of dynamic circuit-breaker rules that open/close based on burn rate signals and tail latency, and (4) prioritized load-shedding policies tied to tenant priority and route criticality.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI definitions documented for endpoint-level latency, tail latency, error rate, and quality (per-prompt quality signal).
Probabilistic degradation algorithm implemented as a service that outputs per-endpoint daily error budget allocations and regional reserve suggestions. API: /v1/slo-allocator.
Circuit-breaker policy prototype integrated into the routing layer that can (a) mark region variant as ejected, (b) route to fallback variant or region, and (c) emit debug traces to the Console.
Load-shedding policy rules able to preemptively drop non-critical work when burn rate exceeds thresholds and to honor tenant priority/SLAs.
Dashboards and alerting for burn-rate, ejection events, and staged rollouts exist in Console (links below).
Runbook updated with step-by-step remediation and rollback guidance for at least two failure scenarios: sudden regional latency spike and model degradation across variants.
technical_notes: SLIs: availability = requests with 200 & latency < 250ms (low-latency routes) or < 1s (batchy routes) measured at edge egress. Error rate = 5xx + model-rejects / total requests. Quality SLI = percent of eval prompts passing acceptance tests derived from per-route promptset; sampled at 1% of traffic for production.
SLO decomposition: use Bayesian shrinkage to allocate error budgets proportional to expected traffic and sensitivity; incorporate tenant weight and model quality sensitivity factor (0.0-1.0).

Burn-rate detection: rolling 1h and 6h burn-rate windows with adaptive thresholds: warn at 0.5x, throttle at 1x, eject at 3x baseline burn. Baseline = historical daily expected burn adjusted for seasonality.

Circuit semantics: CLOSED -> OPEN -> PROBATION. Open when ejection triggers: (a) sustained burn-rate > 3x for 10m, OR (b) p99 latency > configured tail threshold *and* error rate > 0.5%. Probe by sending canary traffic to confirm recovery. Ejection reason tags recorded in trace: burn_rate|latency|quality.

Load-shedding: policy engine accepts prioritized rules: route-level criticality, tenant tier, model-variant score. Shedding decisions are made at the edge router with probabilistic token-bucket drops to avoid synchronized drops.

Traffic re-routing: on ejection, router consults model-variant compatibility table to find a fallback variant with acceptable quality loss; if none, route to next-region warm standby. Warm standby capacity must be >= 10% of peak for critical tiers.
Observability: emit Metric labels: slo_namespace, endpoint, model_variant, region, tenant_tier, ejection_reason. Export traces with trace tag 'slo_alloc_v'.
Data retention: short-term burn metrics at 90d, aggregated baselines at 540d for seasonality.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (experiment): 2-week simulation using production traffic replay to evaluate allocation algorithm. Owners: Diego + Reliability data team.
Phase 1 (canary): deploy allocator + router CB in us-west-2 for a subset of low-risk endpoints (5% traffic). Monitor burn-rate and false positives for 1 week.
Phase 2 (regional rollout): enable in additional regions with gradual traffic ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) and automated abort if critical metrics degrade > 10% vs baseline.
Phase 3 (global): enable multi-region borrowing with policy gates and update Console UI for SLO allocation visibility and manual overrides.
Post-rollout: 30-day observation window, collect operator feedback, refine thresholds and shear parameters.
